findings: Whole DedupeEngine.java reviewed: URL normalization or name-similarity buckets of reading source records; representative selected by metadata score and original order. No byte/perceptual content observation in this file.

Representative score rewards preferred name keywords, enabled flag, filled fields, rule completeness, short names and recency. Such preference is product ranking, not evidence files are interchangeable.

NAME mode inserts groups into one map by normalized first name and ungrouped entries by URL. Potential namespace collision needs NameSimilarity/model contracts and runtime before calling data loss; not reproduced.

Whole NameSimilarity.java read: grouping compares every candidate only to first unused anchor, marks matches used, then quality-sorts group. This is neither connected components nor all-pairs equality; nontransitive similarity can yield order-dependent groups. Static source conclusion, Java runtime not executed.

Similarity is Levenshtein normalized by maximum UTF-16 length plus common-prefix and substring bonuses, capped1; normalized strings<=4 require exact equality. This is name heuristic, not image/file equality.

Two ranking implementations differ: DedupeEngine adds short-name bonus5/3 while NameSimilarity.score omits it despite comment claiming consistency. Group pre-sort and final re-sort can select different representatives; actual fixture not run.

normalize delegates NameCleaner first; its local code does not lowercase final result even though comment says lowercase. Whether upstream cleaner supplies case folding remains unreviewed; no demonstrated case bug claimed.

Whole NameCleaner confirms no case folding; normalize therefore retains English case despite documentation. Cleaner removes zero-width controls and broad emoji/symbol ranges and collapses selected Unicode whitespace. Static source observation, no Java execution.

Complete/standard URL keys preserve nonempty fragment identity labels; requestUrl drops fragment for transport only. Aggressive key intentionally drops scheme/path/query/fragment and www prefix, retaining nondefault port. Thus same-host grouping intentionally does not establish resource/content identity.

Standard query strips configured tracking parameter names after URL-decoding names, sorts retained raw parts, and trims one trailing path slash. Complete key does not sort query. No HTTP requests or content comparisons performed.

Whole source of20 original test methods read: URL errors/count conservation/recency and name normalization/grouping/preferences. These two files lack case-folding, chain/permutation grouping, bucket-key collision and score-consistency cases. Tests not executed.

Five model files wholly read: result/group lists defensive shallow copies, duplicate count sums removed sizes; no constructor invariant that retained+removed+invalid equals originalCount. Existing test checks one finite conservation fixture, not all grouping outcomes.

SourceRecord wraps caller map unmodifiable without copying; nested maps and original owner remain mutable, ruleMap returns nested map directly. Intended ownership convention in comment is not deep immutability. No concurrent mutation observed or runtime test.

SourceRecord has no equals/hashCode override, so runByName grouped HashSet uses object identity; repeated references versus equal-valued objects differ by Java identity semantics. No runtime duplicate-reference case tested.
DedupeMode descriptions explicitly warn aggressive same-domain grouping may remove distinct sources; this is an intended heuristic policy, not a byte-equality contract.

Health producer not reviewed; nonfinite-score admission remains unqualified static concern.
RuleCompleteness is diagnostic only, returns missing search URL/rules and does not delete records. Nonempty rule map passes regardless nested value quality; no semantic rule validation claimed.

parseArray applies25million-character cap after unwrapJson, not raw download byte limit; constructs whole parsed tree. README64MB import claim is a separate boundary requiring fetch/UI review. No memory measurement.

unwrapJson trims by first array/object opener and last matching closer, allowing surrounding nonJSON text; not a JSONP syntax validator. Original index start+i preserves nonobject gaps. ParseResult lists mutable and no total count field; end-to-end accounting pending.

FetchProgress explicitly stores running/cancelled and counters, without constructor consistency checks; state production must be assessed in FetchManager. Immutable scalar container only, not cancellation execution proof.

SystemProxy caches optional Android default proxy in volatile field; init does not clear prior proxy when later no proxy configured or read fails. Reinitialization/network change handling unreviewed, no Android reproduction.

YckUrlPolicy admits configured domain/subdomains and third-party resources by extension; URL-based resource classification does not inspect bytes or establish image identity. Helpers only read, no remote websites requested.

Whole262line FetchManager read:64MiB limit enforced on decompressed stream bytes before writing to accumulator. Confirms network-body boundary, not peak memory bound: whole bytearray/string and unbounded single-thread parse queue retain downloaded bodies. No memory benchmark.

QueueState.takeNext shares current domain bucket across workers; no per-domain lock/worker ownership despite comment claiming same-domain serial. Multiple same-domain URLs can be admitted up to global concurrency. Static control-flow observation, no network runtime test.

parseQueue allocated once and shutdown after workers finish, never recreated by start; reuse of same manager would reject parse submissions. Whether UI creates fresh instance each run remains to inspect.

Queued parser lambdas read mutable manager state/listener rather than captured run generation; cancelled isDone can become true when downloads finish while parsers pending, permitting start before pending callbacks settle. Actual caller scheduling not established.

Parser returns invalid ParseResult without throwing; manager complete(true,records.size) therefore means fetch+parse-return success, not all records valid. Callback throw can call complete twice after first complete; callbacks not failure-injected. No Java execution.
